lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- How the Rule Was Made
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Aguinaldo Ballon | Lesson 4 -- How the Rule Was Made
lesson.grammar_point: passive voice in present, past and future for regulatory decisions

listenings.text: Many investors ask me how our rules are made, so let me explain the process. First, a draft is written by our technical team. Then it is published for public consultation, usually for forty-five days. Last year, our tariff rule received more than four hundred comments. All of them were read, and the main ones were answered in a report. After that, the text was amended and the final rule was approved by the board. The new requirements will be enforced from January. So, when you read a rule from our agency, remember that it was discussed in public before it was published.

Three years ago, a new rule for port terminals was published by the agency. Our client believed that one requirement was illegal, so the rule was taken to court. The first judge disagreed with us, and the rule was enforced for eight months. Then the case was sent to a higher court, and the ruling was overturned. The old framework was applied again. For my client, that was good news. For the investors in the sector, it was terrible, because nobody knew which rule would be applied next year. Since then, the rule has been amended twice, and it is still being discussed.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: to make sure that people follow a rule or a law
a period when the public can send comments on a proposed rule
an official decision made by a court or an agency
to cancel an official decision, usually in a court
a weakness in a rule that allows people to avoid it legally
the set of rules and principles that organize a sector
something that a rule says you must do or have
to change a law, a rule or a contract officially

paras: A new rule for infrastructure is rarely created in one day. First, a draft is prepared by the technical team of the agency. Then a public consultation is opened, and comments are sent by companies, investors, lawyers and ordinary users. In a big sector, hundreds of comments can be received. Each one is read, and the most important ones are answered in a public report.

After the consultation, the text is amended and the final rule is published. At this point, a new requirement usually starts, but not immediately. Companies are given a transition period, often six or twelve months, because new systems and reports have to be prepared. During this period, the rule is not enforced with penalties.

The story does not always end there. Sometimes a company believes that the agency went too far, and the rule is taken to court. If a judge agrees, the ruling can be overturned, and the old framework is applied again. For foreign investors, this is one of the most difficult things to understand: in Brazil, a published rule is not always a final rule.
